newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian envoy leaves for rebel Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russian envoy leaves for rebel Chechnya.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed flew to Chechnya on Thursday for talks with separatist leaders less than a week after signing an ambitious peace deal for the breakaway region.
Interfax news agency said that during the two-day visit Lebed would meet rebel chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov, with whom he signed the accord on Saturday.
The meeting would take place in the village of Novye Atagi, some 25 km (15 miles) to the south of capital Grozny.
It is expected to deal with ironing out problems in implementing the peace deal which defers a decision on Chechen independence for five years.

Though Lebed is President Boris Yeltsin's personal representative in Chechnya, the 65-year-old president, who dropped from sight in late June and is now on holiday near Moscow, has not publicly backed Lebed's peace deal.
The first test of the deal is expected to be on Friday, the fifth anniversary of Chechnya's self-declared independence.
Interfax said Maskhadov has pledged to bar any parade celebrating in Grozny and have only religious ceremonies there.
